name: Crucible Industries Long Arm LA-20 'Verdict'
description:
A heavy anti-materiel railgun designed for engaging hardened targets at extreme range. The LA-20 fires a 6mm depleted uranium penetrator at velocities exceeding Mach 10, generating enough kinetic energy to defeat light vehicle armor at 3 kilometers. The weapon is semi-portable — technically man-carried, but effective deployment requires a stabilization tripod and a two-person crew.

Crucible designed the Verdict for corporate border disputes where armored vehicles and reinforced positions made conventional sniper rifles irrelevant. The weapon's electromagnetic launch system produces a distinctive violet flash and a pressure wave that can be felt by bystanders within 20 meters of the firing position.

The LA-20 has earned its nickname from its absolute lethality against personnel targets. There is no armor system rated for personal wear that can stop a Verdict round. Corporate security advisors simply classify it as an environmental hazard.
legality: Military restricted — heavy weapons authorization required
specifications: caliber: 6mm depleted uranium penetrator effective_range: 500-5,000 meters rate_of_fire: 1 round per 12 seconds capacity: 3-round internal magazine weight: 18.5 kg rifle, 8 kg power unit, 6 kg tripod power_source: Belt-mounted fusion cell, 30 shots per cell
tactical_use: The Verdict is deployed against hardened targets that lighter sniper systems cannot defeat — armored command vehicles, reinforced observation posts, and shielded communications arrays. Its anti-personnel use is technically overkill but sends an unmistakable message. Corporate armies deploy LA-20 teams to establish no-go zones during territorial disputes, as the weapon's extreme range and penetration make any position within line of sight untenable.
cultural_context: In GLMZ's corporate conflict zones, a Verdict shot is called 'the court ruling' — it settles disputes with finality. Lower-tier residents who live near corporate borders have learned to recognize the distant violet flash and the delayed thunderclap that follows. When they see it, they know to stay indoors for days.
story_hooks: A Verdict round punched through a Tier 4 executive's panic room — three walls of reinforced composite, and the round still had enough energy to exit the building. The shooter was never found.
Crucible is testing an LA-20 variant that fires programmable rounds capable of airburst — turning an anti-materiel weapon into an area denial system.

physical_description.visual_profile: A brutalist, angular anti-materiel system dominated by a massive reinforced barrel housing. The silhouette reads as deliberately intimidating — a horizontal dominance with a pronounced muzzle brake that flares like a predator's mouth. The receiver is thick and machined, suggesting immense internal forces. Overall impression: industrial violence made tangible.
physical_description.dimensions: Rifle body: 142 cm length, 8 cm width at receiver, 6 cm height at rail. Barrel: 98 cm with muzzle brake extending to 110 cm total. Tripod base when deployed: 110 cm wide, 85 cm tall when leveled.
physical_description.weight_description: Hefty and purposeful. The 18.5 kg rifle demands respect in hand — balanced but requiring a shooter's full attention. The separate 8 kg fusion cell pack and tripod system mean this is crew-served in genuine field conditions, despite being technically 'man-portable.'
physical_description.primary_material: Reinforced carbon composite receiver with interlocking titanium stress plates. Barrel is progressive-spiral wound exotic alloy designed to channel and direct electromagnetic discharge. Rail system is hardened steel.
physical_description.finish: Matte charcoal composite with brushed titanium accents around barrel nodes. Electromagnetic coil housing shows a subtle iridescent sheen — slight purple undertone from the capacitor matrix visible beneath semi-translucent polymer access panels. Worn spots at the grip reveal bare composite beneath.
physical_description.color_scheme: Charcoal black primary with gunmetal gray rail systems. Titanium silver around coil housings and muzzle brake. Accent stripe of deep indigo running along the left side of the receiver — Crucible Industries brand color.
physical_description.grip_texture: Textured black polymer with subtle knurling. Cool to the touch. The charging handle is wrapped in worn synthetic cord, suggesting field use. Magazine well surround is rougher, almost gritted for gloved operation.
distinctive_features: Muzzle brake with six radial ports and a central aperture — designed to channel violent discharge, creates visible violet corona on firing
Three electromagnetic coil nodes visible along the barrel, each with recessed cooling vents and small status LED arrays (amber/green indicators)
Heavy-duty rail-mounted targeting system with integrated ballistic computer mount (currently empty)
Charging handle with distinctive dual-finger grooves and a small pressure release button
Fusion cell coupling port on right side of receiver — substantial industrial connector with safety interlocks
Magazine well shows brass ejector residue and minor burn scarring consistent with repeated high-velocity discharge
Crucible Industries stamp embossed on left side of receiver, partially obscured by wear
Pressure relief valve on the upper receiver marked with Φ symbol and safety specifications
Subtle carbon scoring around the muzzle brake — heat scarring from plasma discharge
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: Crucible Industries logo (angular C symbol) stamped on the left side of the receiver in small silver lettering. Serial plate mounted on the right side with technical specifications and a manufacturing date stamp. Small warning labels in English and Mandarin around the fusion cell coupling.
physical_description.condition_typical: Well-maintained but combat-experienced. The composite shows minor scratches and dust accumulation from field deployment. Polymer has slight discoloration from heat exposure. The muzzle brake shows carbon scoring that suggests recent use. Minimal corrosion — this is a weapon kept in working condition out of necessity, not pride.
